nodes.statement: navigator.gpu is a [SecureContext] attribute: WebGPU exposure requires a secure context, and the loopback origin 127.0.0.0/8 is potentially trustworthy.

A fallback/software adapter (GPUAdapterInfo.isFallbackAdapter, architecture 'swiftshader') is browser WebGPU API execution on the CPU, never hardware GPU execution; hardware evidence needs a non-fallback adapter.

An adapter is single-use (consumed after requestDevice) and may expire at any time; recovery must start again at requestAdapter; requestDevice on an expired adapter yields a device lost with reason 'unknown'.
A wasm64 module produced by rustc assumes bulk-memory, mutable-globals, sign-ext and nontrapping-fptoint; the executing engine must accept these in addition to i64 addresses.
Toolchain identity is recorded per evidence record and never pinned by the repository; a wasm64/no_std claim is valid for the recorded nightly commit and component set only.
Browser flags that enable a software GPU path are implementation switches documented for GL/WebGL; their effect on WebGPU admission is established only by the executed probe, not by documentation.
ASCII remains the source of record; internal IR may represent but never replace it.
Approved target nodes are not silently removed; unavailable capabilities stay [GAP]/[ERR]/[UNK] in G.
wasm32 fallback is forbidden (project decision, not an upstream requirement).
canonical_base is a git commit object name; a workpiece is a detached linked worktree at that commit; integration is fast-forward only when the canonical head still equals canonical_base.
Station and fixture surfaces are literal prefix sets ('*', 'dir/', or an exact file); glob-looking entries authorize nothing (D9 [GAP]).
Physical browser evidence is a separate class from synthetic/model evidence; the E0 -> E1 sequence must be witnessed physically with no codegen between epochs and the authored source unchanged.

Adapter acquisition is fallible and capability-bearing: requestAdapter can return null; an adapter exposes features/limits; adapters may expire; admission = adapter != null and required features/limits satisfied.
Device loss is part of the lifecycle; backend state includes loss and reacquisition; loss triggers re-observation/replanning.
WGSL is separately governed; shader generation must satisfy current WGSL semantics independently of host API correctness.

Compiler crates use Rust's no_std model: std is not linked; the core prelude applies.
Building core from source requires rust-src, nightly cargo and nightly rustc, and -Z build-std on every invocation; reproducible fixtures must state toolchain and build-std use explicitly.
The rustc wasm64 page is implementation authority for Rust's target, not authority for WebAssembly standards status.
Trustworthiness is computed, not assumed; secure-context-dependent capabilities require a trustworthy environment.
The Threads proposal defines shared-memory/atomic semantics as a distinct implementation family.
Shared-everything threads is separate future machinery; never treated as current Core 3.0 browser semantics.
64-bit address types are current WebAssembly semantics (address types include i32 and i64).
A memory type carries its address type; wasm64 codegen/validation must preserve the intended address type.
The JavaScript Memory descriptor is address-type aware; the host membrane must represent the current descriptor/address model.
Streaming compilation requires a CORS-same-origin, ok, application/wasm response; wrong MIME and non-ok responses must fail admission.
The current JS embedding is agent-local: proposal-based shared Wasm threading is not an unconditional Core+JS backend.
Workers are explicit background execution contexts requiring lifecycle/communication contracts.
hardwareConcurrency reports logical processors potentially available to the UA and can be reduced; never proof of owned cores.
